V.rationale: Visa exhibits excellent fundamental health: Q2 FY26 revenue of $11.23B grew 17.1% YoY with net income of $6.02B, operating margins of ~64%, and net margins of ~52%. The business trajectory is strong with five consecutive quarters of revenue growth from $9.51B to $11.23B. ROE has expanded from ~52% to ~62% over the past year. The asset-light, fee-based model generates exceptional cash flow with minimal capital intensity. However, operating cash flow declined 55.6% QoQ and 35.9% YoY in the latest quarter, which warrants monitoring though this may reflect timing. Valuation is moderately rich: the stock trades at ~28-29x P/E and ~24x forward P/E, above the industry average of 18x but below its own five-year median of ~26x forward. The stock has rallied 21.3% in the past quarter to $362.13, which has compressed some upside. Near-term catalyst exists: Q3 FY26 earnings on July 28, 2026, with consensus EPS estimate of $3.23 and the company having beaten estimates in each of the past four quarters by an average of 3.2%. A new $20B buyback authorization was approved in April 2026. Risks include regulatory headwinds (DOJ antitrust, Credit Card Competition Act), stablecoin competition bypassing Visa rails, and geopolitical tensions affecting cross-border travel. The score reflects a high-quality compounder with strong execution but a valuation that is fair-to-slightly-rich versus its own history, limiting upside to the +0.35 range.
